experiences.name: Sella Ronda
experiences.description: The classic loop around the Sella massif, starting and ending in Corvara. It strings together Pordoi, Sella and Gardena passes with a long hairpin climb and descent on each, and the Dolomite walls close on both sides.

experiences.name: Assietta Ridge and Finestre
experiences.description: A high-mountain crossing of the Cottian Alps: from Sestriere the Strada dell'Assietta ridge road climbs above 2000 m with big views, then the Colle delle Finestre drops to Susa. A good part of it is unpaved and slow going; it is only open in summer and early autumn.

experiences.name: Amalfi Coast Drive
experiences.description: The Strada Statale 163 clings to the cliffs between Sorrento and Salerno, with Positano and Amalfi on the way. It is slow and busy in season, but the sea views and the tight bends are the reason to ride it early in the day.

experiences.name: Lake Como: Como to Lecco via Bellagio
experiences.description: A lake ride along the Como branch to Bellagio on its promontory, then down the western shore of the Lecco branch. It is mostly villages, villas and short lakeside stretches, a relaxed half-day rather than a fast one.

experiences.name: Lake Garda West Shore
experiences.description: The Gardesana Occidentale runs from Riva del Garda past Limone, Gargnano and Salo to the Sirmione peninsula. Tunnels cut through steep rock above the water and lemon-house villages sit between them.

experiences.name: Stelvio Pass
experiences.description: The famous climb from Bormio to the Stelvio summit, then the long switchback descent to Prato allo Stelvio and on through the Val Venosta to Merano. It is among the highest paved roads in the Alps, so pick a clear summer day.

experiences.name: Crete Senesi to Montalcino
experiences.description: From Siena through the bare clay hills of the Crete Senesi, past Asciano and the Monte Oliveto Maggiore abbey, then Buonconvento, to Montalcino. Quiet country asphalt with long open views over the ploughed ridges; a slow, scenic ride rather than a twisty one.

experiences.name: Great Dolomites Road
experiences.description: The traditional Dolomites route from Bolzano to Cortina d'Ampezzo over the Karer Pass, Pordoi and Falzarego. You pass through the Fassa Valley and Arabba with the Sella, Marmolada and Tofane peaks in view the whole way.

experiences.name: Giau, Fedaia and Val Gardena
experiences.description: A quieter Dolomites day from Cortina over Passo Giau and the Marmolada side at Fedaia, then over the Sella Pass and down through Val Gardena to Bolzano. It is a long chain of hairpins with several high passes and little through traffic.

experiences.name: Langhe Wine Roads
experiences.description: A ride through the Langhe vineyard hills from Asti past Barbaresco, La Morra, Barolo and Monforte d'Alba to Mondovi. The roads follow the crests between wine villages and are best in autumn colours or on a quiet weekday.

experiences.name: Riviera di Levante
experiences.description: From Genoa along the eastern Ligurian coast through Rapallo and Sestri Levante, over the Bracco hills to Levanto and the Gulf of La Spezia, ending at Lerici. Short coastal stretches alternate with curvy hill sections above the sea.

experiences.name: Colle di Tenda and the Roya Valley
experiences.description: From Limone Piemonte up the old hairpin road to the Colle di Tenda, then down through Tende and the wild Roya valley to Breil-sur-Roya and Ventimiglia, finishing along the Riviera to Sanremo. A mountain crossing from the Piedmont Alps to the sea, partly through France.

experiences.name: Verona to Venice: Palladian Cities
experiences.description: A culture ride across the Veneto plain from Verona through Vicenza and Padua, then along the Riviera del Brenta with its patrician villas to the lagoon at Venice. The roads are flat and built-up, so the interest is in the cities and villas rather than the corners.

experiences.name: Via Emilia: Piacenza to Rimini
experiences.description: The Roman Via Emilia crosses Emilia-Romagna in a straight line from Piacenza through Parma, Modena, Bologna and Forli to the Adriatic at Rimini. It is a relaxed city-to-city ride with a lot of food stops and plenty of history.

experiences.name: Cisa Pass to Garfagnana
experiences.description: From Parma over the Passo della Cisa into Lunigiana, then through Fivizzano and the Garfagnana valley under the Apuan Alps to Lucca. Quiet Apennine roads, long flowing bends and little traffic away from the pass.

experiences.name: Monti Sibillini and Castelluccio
experiences.description: From Spoleto to Norcia, up to the Castelluccio plateau and over the Forca di Presta to Arquata del Tronto and Ascoli Piceno. High open Apennine scenery with wide views; the plateau is famous for the lentil flowers in early summer.

experiences.name: Gran Sasso and Campo Imperatore
experiences.description: From L'Aquila up to the Campo Imperatore plateau under the Gran Sasso at about 2100 m, then across the plateau past Castel del Monte to Sulmona. Open high-altitude scenery in the heart of Abruzzo, often called Little Tibet.

experiences.name: Rome to Gaeta: Castelli Romani and the Coast
experiences.description: Out of Rome on the Appian Way to the Alban Hills lakes at Castel Gandolfo and Nemi, then across the Pontine plain to Sabaudia and Terracina. The ride follows the Tyrrhenian coast to the bay of Gaeta with sea views on the last stretch.

experiences.name: Umbria and Marche Cities of Art
experiences.description: A tour of hill towns from Urbino over the Apennines to Gubbio, Assisi, Spoleto and Todi, ending at Orvieto. Each stop is a medieval town on a hill, so it is a culture ride at an easy pace on mostly open roads.

experiences.name: Florence to Rome through the Hill Towns
experiences.description: From Florence down the Chiantigiana to Greve and Siena, through the Val d'Orcia at Pienza, then Orvieto and on to Rome. A full day through the classic Tuscan and Umbrian landscape with the cities of art at both ends.

experiences.name: Adriatic Coast: Pesaro to Vasto
experiences.description: A long run down the Adriatic coast: the Conero promontory at Sirolo, Pescara and then the Costa dei Trabocchi fishing platforms before Vasto. Mostly fast coastal roads with the sea on one side and a few curvy stretches at Conero.

experiences.name: Puglia: Trulli to the Heel
experiences.description: From Bari through Alberobello's trulli country and white Ostuni to Baroque Lecce, up the Adriatic coast to Otranto and south to Santa Maria di Leuca. Flat and open with olive groves and stone-walled lanes; the interest is the towns and sea.

experiences.name: Calabria: Tyrrhenian Coast to Reggio
experiences.description: From Scalea down the Tyrrhenian coast through Pizzo and Tropea, past the Costa Viola cliffs at Scilla to Reggio Calabria on the Strait of Messina. Sea views for most of the day and plenty of coastal villages to stop at.

experiences.name: Sicily: Palermo to Taormina via Madonie and Etna
experiences.description: From Palermo along the north coast to Cefalu, then up through the Madonie mountains at Castelbuono and across the interior to Randazzo on the north flank of Mount Etna. Down past the volcano to Taormina. A big day with a lot of changing landscape.

experiences.name: Sardinia: Olbia to Cagliari along the East
experiences.description: The length of Sardinia's east side from Olbia through Dorgali and Baunei, on the Supramonte cliffs above the sea, then south past Villasimius to Cagliari. Mountain road bends inland and coastal views for most of the day.
